items.title: Ring road: stop-and-go waves
items.what: Cars only, one lane, a 1 km ring in exact IDM equilibrium with one vehicle disturbed to half speed; the last 5 of 15 simulated minutes are measured. The disturbance must die out at low density and grow into jams that travel upstream.

headline.label: jam wave speed at 70 and 80 veh/km

reference.text: Empirically observed stop-and-go waves move against the traffic at about -10 to -20 km/h.
reference.source: Kerner and Rehborn 1996 (about -15 km/h); Treiber and Kesting 2013, Traffic Flow Dynamics, Ch. 18; ring experiment after Sugiyama et al. 2008

items.title: Free-flow lane capacity (fundamental diagram)
items.what: Maximum of flow = density x mean speed over homogeneous ring runs of cars.

reference.text: Single-lane capacities of about 1,800-2,400 veh/h for cars (basic segments up to 2,400 pc/h/ln; urban arterials lower).

items.title: Stop-line discharge (saturation flow) at J1
items.what: Standing queues of 24 vehicles are released at J1's stop lines; the headways after the fourth vehicle are averaged (engine/calibration.py).

reference.text: HCM base saturation flow 1,900 pc/h/ln; IRC:SP:41 gives 525 PCU/h per metre of approach width (about 1,840 for 3.5 m). The mix is counted in vehicles, not PCU, so it is lower by construction.

items.title: J2 gap acceptance: minor left turn (merges east)
items.what: The minor movement is saturated (900 veh/h demand); a vehicle enters only if every conflicting priority vehicle is at least the critical gap (6.9 s) from the conflict point. Capacity is compared with HCM's gap-acceptance formula for the measured conflicting flow.

reference.text: c_p = v_c e^(-v_c t_c / 3600) / (1 - e^(-v_c t_f / 3600)) with t_c = 6.9 s, t_f = 3.3 s (four-lane major road, mirrored for left-hand traffic).

notes: New measurement on the current two-lane minor approach. The README's older left-turn table (156 against 287 veh/h) was made with one shared minor lane, before the approach was split. Here the simulation serves MORE than HCM's formula gives. Not isolated: the formula is evaluated with all eastbound through flow as conflicting (HCM uses the near lane for a minor movement onto a four-lane road), the left-turn lane no longer waits behind right-turners, and the formula assumes random arrivals while the real stream is bunched. Treat it as 'not validated against HCM' rather than as agreement.

items.title: J2 gap acceptance: minor right turn (crosses both eastbound lanes)
items.what: The minor movement is saturated (900 veh/h demand); a vehicle enters only if every conflicting priority vehicle is at least the critical gap (7.5 s) from the conflict point. Capacity is compared with HCM's gap-acceptance formula for the measured conflicting flow.

reference.text: c_p = v_c e^(-v_c t_c / 3600) / (1 - e^(-v_c t_f / 3600)) with t_c = 7.5 s, t_f = 3.5 s (four-lane major road, mirrored for left-hand traffic).

items.title: Webster's cycle calculation (J1)
items.what: The fixed-time plan is built from measured saturation flows and start-up losses, ITE intergreens and the default demand; the optimum cycle is recomputed here from the plan's own critical flow ratio and lost time.

rows: critical flow ratios y per phase
applied cycle s (capped at 120 s, IRC:93)

reference.text: Webster's optimum cycle C0 = (1.5 L + 5) / (1 - Y); the applied cycle is limited to 120 s.
reference.source: Webster's formula as implemented in engine/webster.py; cycle cap IRC:93

items.title: Known difference: the J2 right turn serves 64% of HCM
items.what: 132 against 207 veh/h at 980 veh/h conflicting flow. Nothing was tuned to close the gap. Attribution from the same run (saturated right turn):
bullets: Fewer usable gaps than random arrivals (largest): gaps of at least 7.5 s occur 52 times per hour against 127 for a random stream of the same flow; the merged conflicting stream has a headway CV of 1.77 (1.0 for random). Where the bunching comes from is a hypothesis (the J1 signal, the lane drop, the flyover merge); not isolated.
Partly offset: in a bunched stream the gaps that occur are longer, so each usable gap serves 2.5 vehicles against about 1.6 in HCM's formula.

Follow-up headway: consecutive right-turners enter 4.36 s apart against HCM's 3.5 s (the right-turn path is 24.8 m long and curvature-limited to about 21 km/h); worth up to about -20% for the second and later vehicles in a gap.
Small: a vehicle must be at the line when the window opens (2 of 15 windows unused).

reference.source: HCM 6th ed., Ch. 20; README, Known differences from HCM

items.title: Known difference: stop-line saturation flow is about 1,630 veh/h, not 1,900
items.what: Measured, not assumed (a standing queue is released and the headways after the fourth vehicle are averaged). It decomposes for cars at J1's through movement:

rows: steady-state maximum on a ring at J1's desired speed (39 km/h)
steady-state maximum on a ring at a 59 km/h desired speed
J1 queue discharge at a 60 km/h desired speed

bullets: Desired-speed ceiling: for IDM the steady flow is q(v) = v / (L + s*(v)); the (v/v0)^4 term widens the equilibrium gap near v0, so at a 40 km/h urban limit the best steady flow is about 1,766 veh/h.

Start-up transient: a queue is released at a = 1.0 m/s^2 (a comfortable urban acceleration); the first four headways are 4.2, 3.1, 2.8 and 2.7 s against a steady 2.15 s, so the discharge stays about 7% below the steady-state ceiling.

HCM's 1,900 comes from field data at higher speed limits with faster drivers; reproducing it needs both a higher desired speed and a = 1.5 m/s^2, i.e. a different parameter set. Sensitivities: a 1.0 to 1.5 gives +6%, T 1.0 to 1.2 gives -8%, v0 40 to 60 km/h gives +8%.
This is not the motorway 'capacity drop' (jam outflow below free-flow capacity), which appears on the ring road.

reference.source: HCM 6th ed., Ch. 19; README, Known differences from HCM
